title: Slow Cooker Mushroom Barley Soup
description: An earthy, hands-off soup with mushrooms, barley, carrots, and broth.
substitutions: Use quick-cooking barley and add it during the final hour.
Use extra carrots if you do not have celery.

steps.text: Add everything to the slow cooker.
Cook until the barley and vegetables are tender.

cookSteps.text: Add 8 ounces sliced mushrooms, 3/4 cup pearl barley, 2 sliced carrots, 2 sliced celery stalks, 1 diced small onion, 6 cups broth, 1 teaspoon thyme, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on LOW for about 6 hours, until the barley is tender and the soup is thickened.
Stir well, taste, and add salt if your broth needs it before serving.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze up to 3 months. Barley continues to absorb broth, so add a splash when reheating.

title: Sheet-Pan Teriyaki Tofu & Broccoli
description: Crisp-edged tofu and broccoli roasted together with a simple sweet-savory glaze.
substitutions: Use cauliflower instead of some or all of the broccoli.
Use maple syrup instead of honey.

steps.text: Heat oven and mix the glaze.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan if desired.
Whisk 3 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons honey or brown sugar, 1 tablespoon oil, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch if using.
Add 14 ounces cubed tofu and 5 cups broccoli to the pan. Drizzle with the glaze and toss gently to coat.
Spread everything in one layer and roast 22–25 minutes, turning once, until the broccoli is browned at the edges and the tofu is firm.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat in a hot oven or skillet for the best texture.

title: Leftover Pasta Frittata
description: A simple skillet frittata that turns leftover cooked pasta into a sturdy breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
substitutions: Any shape of cooked pasta works, with or without a light sauce.
Add a handful of cooked vegetables if you have them.

steps.text: Heat the skillet and loosen the pasta.

cookSteps.text: Heat the broiler. Warm 1 tablespoon oil or butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat.
Add 2 cups cooked pasta and spread it evenly. Warm for 2 minutes.
Beat 6 eggs with 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Stir in 1/2 cup shredded cheese if using, then pour over the pasta.
Cook without stirring for 5–6 minutes, until the edges are set but the center is still soft.
Move the skillet under the broiler for 2–3 minutes, watching closely, until the center is just set and lightly golden.

storage: Refrigerate wedges up to 3 days. Good warm or at room temperature.

title: Small-Batch Pear Crumble
description: A warm two-serving pear dessert with a quick oat-brown-sugar topping.
substitutions: Use quick oats if that is what you have.

steps.text: Heat oven and add pears to the dish.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Put 2 diced pears in a small baking dish.
Mix 1/4 cup oats, 3 tablespoons flour, 3 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 tablespoons softened butter, and 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon until crumbly.
Scatter the topping over the pears.
Bake 22–25 minutes until the pears are bubbling and the topping is golden.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat briefly before serving if desired.
